title: Pressuring Paul Whiteman to let Bix and Tram play jazz
summary: At a Whiteman concert in New Orleans, Hazel pressed Whiteman for Bix and Trumbauer, and the band finally played jazz.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Yeah. Did you know Bix well?

Yeah, I knew Bix pretty well. Like I tell you, Moore threw that. And then he came down a couple of times when he was with Whiteman. He and Frank Trombauer were with Whiteman. We like broke the thing up. They did a concert, you see. And there was no jazz at all. So after the intermission, we were in the alley side. It was old St. Charles said up there. They've torn it down now, I think. Well, I was delegated to go up and speak to Whiteman and tell him that we wanted to hear some Bix and Tram, you see. So I walked up to him and I told him, and I must have said it in a gangster-like way or something. And he looks at me and he says, well, I'll tell you, all we're going to do when we go back, we're going to play Metropolis and American in Paris. And Trombauer's going to do it in the shoes. You know, these great big long shoes that the clowns and the circuses just get up on the top of those things and walk around. That was in the act. So I told him, I said, now we've got to have some of Bix and Tram or we're going to break this thing up. Like I say, he must have taken me for a gangster. So when they go back in, they get the band all on the stage and everything. He comes out to the footlights and he says, ladies and gentlemen, he says, I have had a lot of requests and a lot of threats for Bix and Tram. And he turns around and he tells them, you're on your own. He walks off stage, you see. So Roy Bog was a piano player, one of the piano players at that time. So he started vamping, singing the blues, you see. So they played that and then they played about three or four things and broke up the house. But if we hadn't have done that, we wouldn't have got one note of jazz out of the whole thing.
You had to coerce Whiteman to get any jazz.
